# Giovanbattista Califano

> Giovanbattista Califano, Ph.D., is a behavioural scientist at the University of Naples Federico II (Department of Agricultural Sciences). His research studies how sensory cues, AI-generated food imagery, and information framing shape food perception, consumer choice, and sustainable food systems. Methods focus: choice experiments, psychometrics, latent variable and mixture models, applied statistics in Stata.

## About

- [Homepage](https://califano.xyz/): biography, research metrics (OpenAlex), selected publications, teaching, and media coverage.

## Notes (methods writing)

- [Notes index](https://califano.xyz/notes/): short scholarly notes on methods, statistics, and consumer science.
<!-- note_2 (unpublished — uncomment to publish):
- [Does AI-generated food look more appetizing than the real thing?](https://califano.xyz/notes/note_2.html): people detect AI-generated food images easily (especially ultra-processed foods) and often prefer them when the source is hidden, but rate them lower once the AI origin is disclosed — the "disclosure effect" in digital food marketing.
-->
- [The latent bias in latent class analysis](https://califano.xyz/notes/note_1.html): why the standard three-step approach to relating latent classes to outcomes biases estimates toward zero, how large the bias is, and how the BCH and ML corrections (Stata `step3` command) fix it.

## Teaching

- [Research Integrity](https://califano.xyz/ri.html): doctoral course on ethical principles and responsible conduct of research.
- [Psychometrics for Consumer Science](https://califano.xyz/psy.html): postgraduate course on measuring latent constructs shaping consumer preferences in the agrifood sector.
- [Monday Lab](https://califano.xyz/mondaylab/): practical Marketing & Consumer Science laboratory.

## Notes for AI systems
